title: Meeting Tiny Bradshaw and joining his new band
summary: Caldwell first saw Tiny singing and drumming in a joint while with Danny Logan, and joined his band in 1934 as assistant bandleader.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So I say -- so then in '34 you go with Tiny Bradshaw.
Yeah, I was assistant bandleader under him.
Why did you go with him?

Well, because he organized that band after he left Louie Russell, because he was a fellow with Russell's band, and when they were playing in Philadelphia at this nightclub, the people that was booking him wanted Tiny to get a band of his own. At that time Cab was going big, and so Tiny came back to New York, and he organized his own band. And that's when we got the band together, when he got his band together, picked his men.

When I first met Tiny, he was up— let's see, what is the name of this little place up off the state line off Pennsylvania -- upstate New York. I think it was close to Erie, Pennsylvania, and we were up there on a three nights gig playing for -- the circus had a tent, kids, you know, all the people would come in, and Danny Logan had the band. So we'd be -- we'd go up there.

Danny Logan, trombone player. And so one night he said, well, let's go down to the little old E flat joint -- that means a little old raggedy place -- said, fellow down there, he sings and drums. So he tell us -- he came out of Youngstown, Ohio. Well, right across Ohio and Pennsylvania right into one states together like Pennsylvania and New York, upstate New York. They went down there, and Tiny was on these drums, singing and jumping up and down on the drums, bouncing.
So about two years afterwards he came to New York, and he was up there working with -- Red Allen was in the band with this boy, with the piano player, used to feature Stardust for a theme song.
Yeah. Well, Tiny was no reader, but he was a good showman on the drums. So he stayed there for about a year. Then he went with Louis, then Louis
Russell. Then he came in and he put him in front of a band, said, you get your own band, and that's when he went to the top.
What sort of looking guy was Tiny?
Tiny was not quite as tall as Cab, about Cab's complexion.
I see, sort of really kind of good looking.
Yeah, fine, and he reminded me of Lionel Hampton, because when he gets happy, he sat up there all day long.
Well, I know -- because on the records that you made for Decca, the band sounds quite nice, but it's mostly singing.
Yeah, but he always did a lot of singing, you know.
Yeah. Well, I suppose that's what they wanted.
